title: Grateful Dead Live at Campus Stadium, UC Santa Barbara on 1974-05-25
source: Recording Info: FOB Audience Recording by Jeremy Witt Preserved in posterity for 36 years by Jay Abrams (jra-sm)   Recording Equipment: Sony TC-152, Sony Mics, BASF 120 minute cassettes, Dolby B Analog to Analog Transfer June 1974: Sony TC-152 -> Teac 1230 - Scotch 150, 7" Reels at 3 3/4 ips Transfer by Jim Blackwood Dec 23 2010 Editing and Mastering by Jamie Waddell on the GEMS Edit Station at 24 bit 96 kHz Weiss-Saracon for 16 bit 44.1kHz conversion   TLH for FLAC8   SBE Free

ai_review.summary: A superb audience (FOB) capture of the legendary May‑25‑1974 Wall‑of‑Sound show with rich low end and standout performances of Scarlet Begonias, Let It Grow, Wharf Rat→Dark Star and blistering Jerry on Jackstraw/Mexicali.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑preserved field tape that delivers the massive bottom end of the Wall of Sound while keeping enough clarity to enjoy every instrument; occasional high‑end muddiness, a brief plane fly‑over in Sugaree and an edit near the end of Wharf Rat are the only blemishes. Musically the show shines – Jerry’s furious leads on Jackstraw and Mexicali, a tight, fast Scarlet Begonias, an intense Let It Grow, and a magical Wharf Rat that blossoms into a Dark Star jam highlighted by Keith’s keyboards. Fans consistently praise the energy, uniqueness and historic vibe of this early‑May ’74 California gig.

ai_rating.rationale: All reviews are 5‑star (one 4‑star) and overwhelmingly positive about both performance and recording; the show is described as iconic with multiple standout moments, and the audio quality is deemed excellent despite minor quirks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Rich bottom end, slightly muddy highs, occasional plane noise (Sugaree) and cross‑phase artifacts; a brief edit near the Wharf Rat ending but overall well‑preserved and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A high‑energy early Wall‑of‑Sound set that builds through tight, fast numbers into a soaring second half; the transition from Wharf Rat into Dark Star is highlighted as a seamless and magical peak.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Blistering, fast and furious leads on Jackstraw and Mexicali; described as 'exploding your mind' and providing the launchpad for vocals.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as 'righteous' in the recording; Phil’s spoken thank‑you at the end of Jackstraw is quoted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's keyboards praised during the Dark Star jam ('Keith!!!').
